Two devices from one talk: a two-tone comparison panel (sage green vs coral red) with hand-drawn geometry, and the same speaker keyed over a deep blue gradient with a translucent mark behind him
items.steal: The split panel does the argument with no words; the keying lets a mark sit BEHIND the subject; black hoodie on saturated ground separates with zero effort

items.use: Two devices from one talk: a two-tone comparison panel (sage green vs coral red) with hand-drawn geometry, and the same speaker keyed over a deep blue gradient with a translucent mark behind him
items.steal: The split panel does the argument with no words; the keying lets a mark sit BEHIND the subject; black hoodie on saturated ground separates with zero effort

items.use: Three task columns floating on near-black, the subject inset bottom-left in a rounded window, three pill bars turning green as work completes.
items.steal: The ground is a product UI, not a backdrop: the interface IS the set. Subject never larger than a fifth of the frame. Green carries progress, never decoration.
items.name: 18-dark-thread-canvas.png

items.use: A serif headline ('Your brain's context window') over a row of ten rounded bars grading green to red.
items.steal: One serif sentence carries the whole idea; a single row of shapes proves it. This is the house move: claim in serif, evidence as geometry.
items.name: 19-serif-claim-pill-scale.png

items.use: A screenshot of a real post, with orange marker highlights and hand-drawn white arrows labelled 'Works' and 'Looks'.
items.steal: Annotation as argument: two arrows and two words explain a product decision. Orange only on the two phrases that matter.
items.name: 20-annotation-arrows.png

items.use: Subject in a rounded window on the left third; a full dark dashboard mock on the right with an orange sun mark above it.
items.steal: The most reusable layout in the set: person left, live-looking artefact right, dotted texture in the lower third to stop the black going flat.
items.name: 21-dashboard-half.png

items.use: 'Personal intelligence agents' in serif, subtitle in sans, a monitor outline with three check-marked rows and a white circle with a pause glyph.
items.steal: Thin white line icons at one weight, one green tick repeated three times. The pause circle is a character, not an icon — a small mascot earns warmth.
items.name: 22-icon-diagram.png

items.use: The same dashboard again, now carrying an orange 'AI-powered' badge, an ask bar and the words 'LLM-powered' set huge under it.
items.steal: Repeat the artefact and add one element: the difference between the two frames IS the explanation. Accent used once per frame.
items.name: 23-orange-badge.png

items.use: 'Projects' in serif over a cloud outline containing an orange sun mark, three crab-glyph nodes and a laptop outline below.
items.steal: A diagram is allowed to be friendly. Two stroke weights (blue cloud, white laptop), orange kept for the brand mark only.
items.name: 24-cloud-diagram.png

items.use: A mock handwritten note showing HTML/CSS next to a torn-paper 'Video model' card with a red X, plus a green check on 'Much cheaper'.
items.steal: When the argument is a comparison, leave the interface entirely: paper, marker, torn edge. Tactile beats polished for one beat, then back.
items.name: 25-paper-collage.png

items.use: Six app icons in a 3×2 grid with names under them, on black, subject still at left.
items.steal: Icons as evidence in a taxonomy frame. Nothing else on screen: no paragraph, no bullet, no arrow. The grid is the sentence.
items.name: 26-app-icon-grid.png

items.use: The subject alone, full frame, real room, real window, hands moving, no graphics at all.
items.steal: The reset shot. After five designed frames, one honest one buys back trust — and it is free to produce.
items.name: 27-full-room-honest.png

items.use: Subject fills the left half in a rounded window; an iPhone mock sits right with a green call button and three pill buttons — Delivery, Supplier, Booking.
items.steal: Simulate the product and footnote it (*live demo simulation). Green means 'capability', orange means 'attention' — never the same colour twice.

items.use: Two cut-paper buildings: a cream shopfront with an 'Offline' sign and one clerk, facing a blue-awning storefront with a browser window and four customers.
items.steal: The comparison IS the picture: two buildings, two eras, two palettes. Faceless paper figures sidestep casting entirely — the model village argues better than a chart.

items.use: Dark isometric city block with an orange glowing route from a blue RoboLabs pin to a yellow building; a floating card reads 'Stripe Pay — SENT $500, Transfer fee $0, Just announced 27 Oct'.
items.steal: An invisible transaction becomes physical as a line on a map. The numbers live in a floating card; the motion is the line drawing itself.

items.use: Subject large left; right, a browser mock of a real-looking Shopify store with product photo, price and a 'Buy with Shop Pay' button.
items.steal: Evidence is allowed brand colour: the real logo earns trust a drawn one cannot. Crop the mock like a screenshot, keep one button hot.

items.use: Full desktop app on screen — mascot avatars in the sidebar, a pink chat bubble asking for a gift under $50, three product cards as the answer, settings toggles right; subject inset bottom-left.
items.steal: The interface carries the story: bubbles for conversation, cards for the answer, chips for labels. The person shrinks to an inset so the product can be the star.

items.use: Isometric: a phone stand carrying a card labelled 'you', a blue shop building labelled 'the shop', Apple Pay and G Pay marks, and a stand-in card number.
items.steal: Two plinths, two parties, one abstract idea made concrete. Lowercase labels under objects — no arrows needed.

items.use: Orange vault icon, a white bot face, dotted connector lines running to 'Sign in' and 'Checkout' cards filled with orange dots standing in for passwords.
items.steal: Security explained as objects joined by dotted lines. Orange only on the vault and the secrets, so the eye learns what matters in one frame.

items.use: Serif 'Agentic payments' on a black plate taped to the wall, an orange cut-paper credit card, a blue paper bag and a white bot face; torn newspaper scraps in the corners.
items.steal: Paper collage says 'concept, not screenshot'. A taped serif plate is the cheapest chapter title there is.

items.use: '10 Updates' in white bold; three cards lit with an orange outline under a 'Business' label in serif, then six unlit cards, then the tenth below. Each card carries a mascot glyph and a number.
items.steal: A chapter menu as a board of tokens: shape instead of icon, number instead of word. The first three glow because they are the ones that matter to a business owner.

items.use: The same board without the glow, the Business label or the emphasis — every card equal.
items.steal: The lit/unlit pair is the motion. One frame gains emphasis and the eye follows without a single arrow; build the pair, not the animation.

items.use: 'One memory, one context' in serif; three isometric plinths — Claude on yellow, ChatGPT on green, Grok Bot on blue — wired by dotted orange lines to a central stack of orange plates.
items.steal: The circuit board: outer nodes wear the other people's brand colours, the accent is spent only on the thing being added. Dotted wires, no arrows.

items.use: A title caught mid-arrival, soft and out of focus behind the bot face; subject large in a rounded window.
items.steal: Titles move. A still from a transition shows text arriving blurred and resolving — stop designing static title cards and design the 400ms that lands them.

items.use: The 10 Updates board with 07 lifted, tilted in 3D and ringed in orange while the rest sit flat.
items.steal: Position without a cursor: one card rotates and gains a ring, and the eye knows exactly where we are. No arrow, no highlight bar.

items.use: Same 10 Updates board, first three cards glowing amber under a Business label; the rest sit equal and flat.
items.steal: Emphasis is a property of the frame, not an effect added on top — the lit trio and the flat six are the same component with one flag.

items.use: A dark card headed PROMPT holding a monospace prompt, orange COPY and outlined FULLSCREEN; beside it an iPhone showing the same words as a bubble; Calendar and Reminders icons wearing green ticks; an orange 'Take a screenshot!' pill.
items.steal: Show the actual prompt as a copyable artefact — proof instead of paraphrase. Green ticks on the app icons do the 'it worked' job.

items.use: Subject large left; a Home icon and a Location icon floating at label size; the phone mock empty beside them.
items.steal: App icons are allowed to be props: unboxed, large, label underneath. The phone stays the hero.

items.use: 'Chat' in serif, a wireframe chat window drawn in squiggle lines with an orange border and an orange circular X badge; subject on the right.
items.steal: Squiggles mean 'text, not readable' and cost nothing — no lorem ipsum, no fake copy. One orange badge is all the UI furniture needed.

items.use: A bright white dashboard and share sheet floating on black, cursor included; the subject reduced to a small inset bottom-left.
items.steal: Contrast does the framing: a white artefact on black needs no border. The presenter can shrink to thumbnail when the modal is the point.

items.use: 'Page' in serif with a solid green circle tick beside it; a white page mock below showing weekly sales, three stat cards and one bar picked out in blue.
items.steal: A serif noun plus one green tick reads as 'done, real, shipped'. One coloured bar proves the chart without a caption.

items.use: Full white app UI: a sidebar of coloured blob mascots with two eyes — GROKO, SHOPO, TRAVO, FITO, GIFTO, MAILO — a client list, and a weekly checklist with green ticks and a black GROKO pill on the row it touched.
items.steal: Each agent is a colour and a shape, not an icon — the roster becomes the navigation. A named pill marks the row the agent acted on.

items.use: Real jungle footage reduced to a centred plate with blurred edges, the presenter cut out bottom-left and overlapping the plate's border.
items.steal: The plate is a frame inside the frame, and the subject crossing its edge is what makes it feel shot rather than assembled. Blur does the letterboxing for free.

items.use: The same composition with the footage filling the frame: tiger in the trees, presenter small in the corner.
items.steal: When the footage earns it, let it run full bleed and keep the presenter small. One size of subject per beat, never two heroes.

items.use: Jay in his own room, full frame, window light, wallpaper and a picture behind him, hands in shot. No graphic at all.
items.steal: The reset again: after a run of designed frames, one unadorned room shot buys back trust. Cheapest frame in the film and the one people remember.

items.use: A single product mark on the black field with a dotted orange arc curving away from it and ending in a filled dot.
items.steal: An arrow without an arrowhead: dotted curve, filled circle at the head. It reads as motion even frozen, which is why it survives as a still.

items.use: The panel arrives as an empty rounded outline with one film glyph and a title; nothing inside it yet.
items.steal: Draw the container before the contents. Half a second of empty frame tells the viewer where to look, so nothing has to be announced.

items.use: Vendor tiles land inside the panel, each a rounded square with a label under it, spaced evenly on a dotted grid.
items.steal: Tiles are evidence: real product marks in their own colours, one label each, equal size. No badges, no borders, no glow.

items.use: The panel fills to five tiles; the composition does not change, only the count.
items.steal: Keep the frame and change one number. Every added tile is a beat, and the viewer reads growth with no voice-over needed.

items.use: A rounded card flies in over the panel's top-right corner — orange label MY EARLIER VIDEO, a still from that video, and its title.
items.steal: Cross-reference without leaving the frame: a small card carries the older video, labelled in the accent so it is read as a pointer, not a graphic.

items.use: A real post on a black card with orange highlight bars behind the key sentences; on the right, squiggle bars routing along dotted lines to a bolt icon and a brain icon.
items.steal: Quote with a highlighter, then draw the mechanism beside it. The post carries the authority, the diagram carries the explanation, and each is useless alone.

items.use: Developer mode drawn as a machined panel: serif title, a metal dial ringed with orange LEDs labelled EFFORT low-to-max, a row of model tiles with one lit, tiny screws and a halftone grid.
items.steal: One physical object explains a settings screen better than the settings screen. Screws, LEDs and a serif title cost nothing and read as craft.

items.use: Twelve recent thumbnails of one channel: the same man, the same orange tee, the same neutral expression — a different science image and a different three-word phrase each time.
items.steal: Repeatable packaging: the face and the shirt never change, so only the headline and the object are invented per video. That is a system, not a style.

items.use: The same grid continued: identical pose, identical crop, new phrase, new object.
items.steal: Count the words — never more than four, always heavy condensed caps with a hard shadow. The phrase names the surprise; the image carries the proof.

items.use: Anton cut out in the same waist-up pose as every episode, with the episode's subject photo — the Chernobyl plant — behind him.
items.steal: The background is the episode, not the room. One lighting setup, one camera, one shirt; the subject swaps the plate behind him.

items.use: A full-frame aerial of the exclusion zone, forest regrowing around the reactor.
items.steal: When the place is the story, the place fills the frame and he disappears entirely rather than sitting in a corner.

items.use: A microscopy plate of nematodes, full frame, unannotated.
items.steal: Figures stay whole: no boxes, no arrows, no zoom unless the paper needed one.

items.use: A published paper as a page — journal masthead, title, authors, abstract — legible at frame size.
items.steal: Show the source as a source. The masthead is the credibility, so it is never cropped off.

items.use: A dark anatomical diagram of the calf and venous valves glowing red on near-black.
items.steal: One diagram, one idea, dark ground. Accent lives inside the diagram, not on top of it.

items.use: Anton in the same pose with a wolf standing behind him in snow.
items.steal: The plate can be alive — a subject photo with depth beats a flat colour and costs one image search.

items.use: The PrimeTime cut out against a flat blue gradient with a wireframe mark; grey tee, headphones, mic. No room in any of the 54 frames sampled.
items.steal: A permanent set built once. The whole video is made by swapping what appears beside him.

items.use: A social post fills the frame; he shrinks to a small inset in the corner, still cut out.
items.steal: The artefact takes the frame and the presenter becomes a thumbnail. Never two equal subjects side by side.

items.use: A mathematical statement set large on a dark card, him small in the corner.
items.steal: Set the proof as type rather than a screenshot of a PDF.

items.use: An article page at readable size with him inset — the source is the picture.
items.steal: Cite on screen, not in the description: the viewer sees the page they would have had to find.

items.use: Same pose, same tee, a tablet with a blue screen held at chest height, heart imagery behind him.
items.steal: The prop. A tablet or a folded paper gives the hands a job and makes a static shot read as work rather than a pose.

items.use: A grey anatomical plate with soleus and gastrocnemius lettered and arrowed, white ground, red labels.
items.steal: When a diagram must be annotated, annotate the source image rather than redrawing it — the letters are the argument.
